record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Airtanker systems behave like spatial queueing systems in which fires arrive over time and aircraft serve multiple incidents per day, so static deployment models are inadequate. The open question is how to couple spatial, time-dependent queueing models with tractable optimization methods to support both initial daily airtanker deployment and dynamic redeployment as fire activity evolves.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21 How can we develop spatial time-dependant queueing models that can be coupled with tractable optimization models to be used to help determine how to best deploy airtankers at the start of each day and how to re-deploy them as the day progresses?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an airtanker deployment system modeled as a spatial, time-dependent queueing system in which fire incidents arrive stochastically according to rates that vary in both space and time, and a finite fleet of airtankers act as mobile servers that travel from bases to fires and may serve multiple incidents per day, with service (travel plus suppression) rates depending on the spatial configuration. Let a day be partitioned into time periods, and let the system state include the locations of airtankers, ongoing fires, and the realized history of arrivals.

Develop a spatial, time-dependent queueing model of this system together with an optimization framework, coupled to the queueing model, that is computationally tractable and produces:
(i) an initial daily deployment of the airtanker fleet to a set of candidate bases at the start of each day, minimizing an appropriate operational performance measure (e.g., expected response time, expected number of fires escaping initial attack, or expected damage); and
(ii) a dynamic redeployment policy that updates the locations of airtankers during the day as new fire activity is observed, again optimizing the same performance measure.

The problem is to construct such a coupled queueing–optimization methodology and to establish its tractability and performance guarantees.
artifact.category_tag: Spatial queueing and stochastic optimization for wildfire response
artifact.status_search_result: Existing work (e.g., the IAAS spatial time-dependent multi-server queueing model and associated deployment heuristics) addresses initial daily airtanker deployment, but a fully tractable integration of spatial time-dependent queueing with optimization that also handles dynamic intra-day redeployment does not appear to have been resolved. The problem is therefore best described as still open, with partial progress on the static daily deployment side.

status_evidence.title: A Time-Dependent Spatial Queueing Model for the Daily Deployment of Airtankers for Forest Fire Control
status_evidence.snippet: IAAS model: spatial time-dependent multi-server queueing system used with a heuristic for daily airtanker deployment.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on static daily deployment via a spatial time-dependent queueing model coupled with a heuristic, but dynamic intraday redeployment is not fully addressed.

status_evidence.title: The use of aircraft tracking GPS data to develop models of the use of airtankers in forest fire management
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work develops empirical service-time models for airtankers, suggesting ongoing research rather than a closed solution.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues on modeling airtanker operations, indicating the coupled queueing-optimization redeployment question remains open.
